leads.summary: Open PR #9520's bounded window-flush wait conflicts with this shutdown's fixed two-second poweroff
leads.consequence: If both features are retained without reconciling the sequencing, #9520's --wait (up to 10s) cannot run to completion before this PR requests poweroff after 2s; applications still flushing may lose state. Its new system-shutdown-test.sh also fails with this PR's shutdown script because it requires a --on-active timer greater than the close-all timeout, and this script has none. Both PRs modify the shutdown file, so the exact merged code still depends on conflict resolution.
leads.triage: factual, verified by coordinator via gh (PR open, head ad0802f3, shutdown uses 15s timer + close-all --wait)

leads.summary: Open PR #10353's session-exit marker would remain set if inhibition or poweroff fails after scheduling
leads.consequence: If #10353's prepare-exit is retained before scheduling during the merge, this PR's asynchronous worker can fail acquiring a logind inhibitor or requesting poweroff after systemd-run already returned success; its notification/error handler never calls omarchy-session cancel-exit. Session restore then stays in exiting mode: automatic snapshots stop, and manual restore immediately skips records until cancel-exit or a new session. Any later forced poweroff can restore an out-of-date snapshot. The shutdown file conflicts between the two PRs, so this is conditional on preserving the upstream prepare-exit hook rather than a claim about either PR in isolation.
leads.triage: factual, verified by coordinator (77ad4d53 shutdown:8,12; session.py:74,130,222,225) and Opus self-check (opt-in service, cleared at next login)

leads.summary: Open PR #12254's shared system-power fixture expects obsolete shutdown calls
leads.consequence: If the logout test additions from #12254 are merged without updating its common shutdown assertion, that test fails: its shutdown case expects a --on-active=2s systemctl timer plus synchronous OSD, state, window and sleep calls, while this PR schedules --inhibit and does those other calls inside the later transient service. Keep its logout checks but use this PR's separate shutdown worker assertions.

flags.claim: The same ordering also means a normal power-off cannot raise a false "Shutdown failed".
flags.why: Too absolute. The main-PID-first stop ordering (src/core/unit.c:5064-5086, sandbox emulation 20/20 in opus/review-plan/runs/20260927T093946Z-fe4405d0/output/sigterm/summary.tsv) only rules out a false notification caused by systemd stopping this service during power-off. My own report lists a narrow case where a normal power-off can still be accompanied by one: a second Shut Down while the first PowerOff is held by shutdown delay inhibitors gets 'Action poweroff already in progress' (logind-dbus.c:2321-2325), and its wrapper notifies while the machine powers off. This is also an inconsistency inside my final-report.md (R1 paragraph vs 'Checked and not reported').

flags.claim: The marker stops automatic session snapshots and makes restore skip saved applications.
flags.why: Mechanism correct at #10353 head 77ad4d5 (default/session/session.py:74 automatic save returns; :130 restore loop breaks), but qualifiers are lost. The marker is only set when #10353's opt-in omarchy-session.service is active (prepare-exit returns early otherwise, session.py:196). It lives under $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR (session.py:16), and the next graphical login's startup() removes it (session.py:165-170). So the effect lasts for the rest of that session, not indefinitely.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13076#issuecomment-5807449824) and the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13076#issuecomment-5841830403), checked at `eaaca77`.

**Verified:** both earlier points are resolved. One new low-likelihood robustness point is noted below.

| Earlier point | Status at `eaaca77` |
|---|---|
| Shutdown silently dropped if `Inhibit` is refused (for example, a lid suspend winning the lock-acquisition race) | **Resolved.** Any `systemd-inhibit` failure now sends a critical "Shutdown failed" notification and keeps the original exit status |
| Optional test: nothing checked that preparation cannot delay power-off | **Resolved.** The new blocked-window-close test fails in 3 of 3 runs when the trailing `&` is removed |

**Verified** for the notification path:
- A refused `Inhibit` makes `systemd-inhibit` exit 1, which runs the new `|| { ... }` block.
- The saved status survives a failing notification, as the new test 8 checks. Diagnostic mutants that drop the notification, force exit 1, take the status from the notification or always notify were each caught by the head test.
- In the Omarchy shell, critical notifications do not expire, and the default `omarchy-action` sender bypasses Do Not Disturb. The message is therefore still on screen after a lid-triggered suspend and resume. The race still cancels the shutdown, but the user is now told to retry.
- The same branch also reports a rejected `systemctl poweroff`. At the earlier head, that case closed windows and then failed silently.
- The four verified notes from the earlier review still hold with `systemd-inhibit` moved inside the service. These are the lid lock choice, the lock counting as active from a `systemd-run --user` service, the lock not blocking the power-off request, and `Type=exec` still returning scheduling failures to the caller.

**Author claims:**
- The failure notifications and the blocked-window-close regression test are confirmed.
- The test file emits exactly 8 `ok` lines. It passed in 10 of 10 sequential and 24 of 24 concurrent sandbox runs.
- The "real-systemd checks" were not reproduced.

### Worker path now comes from the service environment

At the earlier head, the caller's shell expanded `"$OMARCHY_PATH/bin/omarchy-system-shutdown" --inhibited`. It now expands inside the transient service, so it uses the user manager's `OMARCHY_PATH`:

```text
caller:  systemd-run ... "$OMARCHY_PATH/bin/omarchy-system-shutdown" --inhibit      <- caller's OMARCHY_PATH
service: systemd-inhibit ... "$OMARCHY_PATH/bin/omarchy-system-shutdown" --inhibited  <- user manager's OMARCHY_PATH
```

`bin/omarchy-restart-shell` notes that these two can differ after `omarchy-dev-link` or `omarchy-dev-unlink`, because the user manager keeps the environment from session start.

**Impact:** low likelihood, from source and a stubbed emulation, not reproduced on a real system. In that window, Shut Down runs one copy's wrapper and another copy's worker. If the other copy has been removed, `systemd-inhibit` cannot start the worker. The user then sees "Shutdown failed" on every attempt until re-login or reboot.

**Suggested change:** use `"$0" --inhibited`. The service runs the script by the absolute path the caller expanded, so both levels stay on the same copy, as at the earlier head. This variant passed the PR test in a sandbox run.

**Optional notes:**
- If the unit is stopped from outside, for example when `RuntimeMaxSec=30s` expires, systemd signals the `--inhibit` shell first. The shell exits before its `||` block, so no notification is sent. A sandbox emulation showed this in 20 of 20 runs. With default polkit rules, this needs a hung component. The same ordering also means systemd stopping the service during a normal power-off cannot raise a false "Shutdown failed".
- `bin/omarchy-system-reboot` keeps the base timer design. From source, logind refuses a queued reboot the same way while a lid suspend is pending. This is outside the PR's stated scope.
- Open PRs #9520, #10353 and #12254 also edit `bin/omarchy-system-shutdown` or `test/shell.d/system-power-test.sh`, and assume the base timer structure. For example, #10353 clears its session "exiting" marker only when `systemd-run` itself fails. If it is combined with this PR, a refused `Inhibit` inside the new service would leave that marker set while the session keeps running. When #10353's opt-in session service is active, the marker stops automatic session snapshots and makes restore skip saved applications until the next login.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of both changed files at `eaaca77`, their callers, `omarchy-notification-send` and the shell notification plugin, and systemd v261.3 logind, `systemd-inhibit` and `systemd-run` code (key paths cross-checked against v262). The PR's `test/shell.d/system-power-test.sh` ran in an isolated sandbox with stubbed power commands, alongside diagnostic mutants of the shutdown script, the earlier-head and base scripts, and a stop-signal emulation. No real `systemctl`, `systemd-inhibit`, logind, polkit, notification daemon, lid events or hardware were exercised. The worker-path point rests on source and a stubbed emulation. The reboot note is from source only. Related open PRs were read at their current heads.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical follow-up review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
